question.prompt: \(A\) can do a piece of work in \(9\) days. \(B\) is \(50\%\) more efficient than \(A.\) The number of days it takes \(B\) to do the same piece of work is:

solutions.explanation:
Efficiency here means the amount of work completed per day. Being \(50\%\) more efficient means that \(B\) completes \(1+\frac12=\frac32\) times as much work per day as \(A\).

Thus, in \(2\) days, \(B\) completes as much work as \(A\) completes in \(3\) days. The whole job takes \(A\) three such \(3\)-day portions, since \(9=3\cdot3\). Therefore \(B\) needs
\[
3\cdot2=6\text{ days},
\]
choice C.
solutions.title: Compare equal amounts of work
